items.title: 68437_Charles Thompson oral history interview
items.q: And from then on I learned many things from Art Tatum.

ctx.x: I was very, very studiously learning these songs, and learning progressions and I was sitting there playing one

night, alone, or with a drummer, or some one or two musicians, at this jam session, and I was trying to play 'Sweet Lorraine,' and I was playing it to the best of my ability, which wasn't correct, very evidently. And I got this voice behind me which I recognized to be Art Tatum. It was the most frightening thing I'd ever heard in my life, when it first happened. He said, oh, Charlie, that's not the way it goes, (let me show you.) He sort of suggested that I slide over and he sat down and he showed me how to play…

Now, this is something that -- a rare occasion that a man so great and so wonderful would take the time. You know, like a lot of guys would either make gesture of it or try to make a fool or something like that, or embarrass you by it. You know, but the man was just so gentle and kind, and he showed me why I was wrong and showed me how to play it right. And from then on I learned many things from Art Tatum.
